newsitem.title: USA: Russian Prime Minister criticizes U.S. trade policy.
newsitem.headline: Russian Prime Minister criticizes U.S. trade policy.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday criticized some U.S. trade policies, saying they have hurt Russia's economy.
"The structure of international trade is still not balanced," Chernomyrdin said through a translator in a speech to business executives in San Francisco.
He criticized the U.S. Jackson-Vanik amendment, which blocks Most Favored Nation trading status for any country that does not have open emigration policies.

Chernomyrdin said the U.S. has imposed "discriminatory" anti-dumping tariffs on some goods and has restricted the sale of supercomputers. Other policies were "as separated from mutual fair trade as Siberia is from California," he said.
Chernomyrdin called on U.S. investors to set up regional mutual funds focusing on the Russian Far East and other sectors of the Russian economy.
"We urge you to go to Russia. To be bolder. We know you know how to do that," he told the San Francisco Chamber of Commerce.
After his speech, Chernomyrdin met privately with California Gov. Pete Wilson. Wilson's office said they discussed U.S. trade issues and business relations between Russia and California.
Chernomyrdin is scheduled to travel to Beijing later this week for talks with Chinese officials.
